{"id":"KHA-24","title":"Verify browser-local chess adjudication solver portability and resource limits","description":"## Question

Can a pinned specialized chess unwinnability solver run wholly inside the required browsers with usable resource limits, cancellation, and honest exact/unknown outcomes?

The owner explicitly chose to keep exact dead-position and position-sensitive timeout rules, rather than accept rare material-based exceptions. This research unblocks [Choose the application architecture and data boundaries](<https://linear.app/kamkm/issue/KHA-13/choose-the-application-architecture-and-data-boundaries>), using [the dependency research](<https://linear.app/kamkm/issue/KHA-22/verify-chess-rules-board-accessibility-and-dependency-licenses>) as the baseline.

Investigate CHA-Solver 3.0.0 at commit 3484c7e65247003fac8705a9290dc2b5d0978b94 first. Build a disposable browser-local WASM/worker probe if feasible. Verify actual target build, dependencies, FEN/coordinate/color handling, and result distinctions. Reuse prior locked-wall, asymmetric wall, bare-king/rook, and knight/rook fixtures; verify mating witnesses locally without exposing them to a model. Add justified stress, invalid-input and unknown-path controls. Record build/tool versions, artifact and compressed sizes, licenses, latency/memory observations, tested environments, and untested targets.

Use Web Workers or an equivalent isolated browser execution approach to study cancellation and stale-result fencing without blocking rendering or clocks. Termination/budget exhaustion is unknown, never proof of mate or inability to mate. Do not solve timeout unknowns by silently changing the product rule or freezing its clock. Identify deployment constraints such as COOP/COEP, threads, SharedArrayBuffer, CSP, and mobile memory only when actually relevant. Required native acceptance targets are Windows Chrome/Edge/Firefox, macOS Safari, iOS Safari, Android Chrome; document actual coverage honestly.

Keep experiments and raw evidence under experiments/browser-adjudication-solver/ and a cited report at research/browser-adjudication-solver.md. No production integration, backend adjudication, live providers, credentials, paid services, or weakening of requirements. Source soundness/general completeness is a separate concurrent research ticket; coordinate through the parent, not shared edits.","status":"In Progress","updatedAt":"2026-10-16T00:39:19.222Z","url":"https://linear.app/kamkm/issue/KHA-24/verify-browser-local-chess-adjudication-solver-portability-and"}

The owner selected "Keep exact rules; research solver" on 2026-10-16. The proposed material-based MVP exceptions were not accepted.

Preserve complete dead-position detection and the position-sensitive timeout rule from [Define the MVP match lifecycle](https://linear.app/kamkm/issue/KHA-11/define-the-mvp-match-lifecycle), including valid custom starting positions. Do not infer mating possibility from an unknown solver result, a fast helper returning false, lack of a found mate, or ordinary optimal-play tablebase WDL. Do not settle a provisional win and rewrite it later.

Continue with focused research into a browser-local specialized solver. Verify actual browser/WASM portability and bounded resource behavior separately from the source-level soundness, coverage, input assumptions, and undecided-result path. A successful sample is not evidence of complete coverage. The browser remains responsible for rules, clocks and match results; no hosted chess adjudication or AI generation relay is authorized.

No new question is pending. Existing free-tier, delegated-license and unsynced-local-continuation choices remain settled. Both factual research tickets are now Done with cited reports, reproducible evidence and verified attachments:
- [Browser persistence, clock recovery, and managed sync hosting](https://linear.app/kamkm/issue/KHA-23/verify-browser-persistence-clock-recovery-and-managed-sync-hosting)
- [Chess rules, board accessibility, and dependency licenses](https://linear.app/kamkm/issue/KHA-22/verify-chess-rules-board-accessibility-and-dependency-licenses)

The latter reproduces a real conflict with the current lifecycle promise to detect all dead positions and determine possible mate on every timeout. Both standard rules libraries miss a completely explored locked pawn wall; a specialized native solver has useful results but explicitly unknown outcomes and unverified browser support.

The owner is being asked one consequential question: accept documented rare draw/timeout exceptions for the MVP, or retain the exact every-position requirement and investigate a specialized browser-local solver. The recommendation is a documented, bounded material-based policy for the MVP. The question explicitly disclosed that a locked pawn wall might not auto-draw and some unusual timeouts might be scored as a loss rather than a draw. No answer is recorded yet. Do not silently amend the lifecycle requirement, assume a generic helper is complete, or mark architecture Done while this is unanswered.

Already settled: managed free tiers initially with paid upgrades returned to the owner; agent-chosen license default with no owner preference; account play may continue locally as unsynced, with conflicts preserved separately rather than overwriting synced history. The next architecture resolution should make routine stack/storage/auth/clock defaults concrete and record evidence limits.","attachments":[],"createdAt":"2026-10-16T00:35:29.867Z","updatedAt":"2026-10-16T00:35:29.813Z","parentId":null,"resolvedAt":null,"quotedText":null,"author":{"id":"45fdeba7-e6d5-4b71-912f-02932bc83a91","name":"khalil abdalmjeed"},"onBehalfOf":null},{"id":"b94b7653-aa8d-411c-af60-c7fe185b6ce4","body":"## Confirmed offline continuation policy

The owner selected "Continue locally, preserve conflicts" after the hosting research identified the offline-writer tradeoff.

When account sync is unavailable, the current device may continue locally with a clear unsynced warning. Its continuation is pending cloud acceptance. Another device may explicitly take over by advancing the hosted ownership epoch from the last acknowledged checkpoint. If the disconnected continuation conflicts, retain it separately and do not overwrite the accepted synced line, its Undo state, or a final result.

On reconnect, compare ownership epoch and expected revision before replaying the outbox. Publish pending work only when its base is still accepted; never use last-write-wins or silently merge chess branches. A divergent continuation remains available as a saved conflict record/export; continuing it as its own game must be explicit, with its provisional result distinguished from the accepted account game's result.

The chess clock continues through disconnection, pending sync, takeover, and conflict recovery. This clarifies the prior strict-one-writer wording: the cloud has one accepted history and one current cloud epoch; a disconnected browser may temporarily produce a clearly pending local continuation without knowing its epoch was revoked. This policy cannot promise one active browser/provider request globally, immediate knowledge of takeover offline, or automatic upstream cancellation. These are accepted consequences of the owner's choice, not a hidden weakening of the synced history.

Carry this policy into the match-lifecycle specification and final acceptance. No implementation or multi-device acceptance has run.","attachments":[],"createdAt":"2026-10-16T00:29:53.092Z","updatedAt":"2026-10-16T00:29:53.083Z","parentId":null,"resolvedAt":null,"quotedText":null,"author":{"id":"45fdeba7-e6d5-4b71-912f-02932bc83a91","name":"khalil abdalmjeed"},"onBehalfOf":null},{"id":"91ca92e6-05ba-48b8-b415-d034d0bedc36","body":"## License default delegated

The owner answered "I don't really care about that" when asked whether closed-source reuse should be permitted. This records no preference for permissive versus copyleft distribution, rather than an explicit owner selection of a named license.

Use MIT as the initial default for the project's own code, consistent with the owner's standing delegation of routine defaults. Choose compatible dependencies, preserve third-party licenses and attribution, and document the license of the final combined distribution. Do not describe a GPL-covered combined work as MIT-only. If the evidence favors a copyleft dependency, evaluate and record a compatible distribution choice without asking the same preference question again.

The selected architecture still waits on the two research tasks. {"comments":[{"id":"94aa261c-0c01-4973-b0de-73fc2c455782","body":"## Resolution

The cited report "Chess rules, board accessibility, and dependency licenses" and its reproducible evidence bundle are attached. Research source `47b57a492f61c5675301fb3e4dd33fa4d79930de` was integrated as `27a53c1`, at `research/chess-dependencies.md` and `experiments/chess-dependencies/`.

Attachment `d6c8fe58-5781-4da3-b737-3a765a7a2486` is the report, SHA-256 `d459fa7c88eb2b9a2031fee71eadf82e29450d57861eabb997b9175a75874050`, 49,752 bytes. Attachment `b838d3c8-6f96-4c70-80ea-1ea6aca0f6c5` is the 27-file evidence bundle, SHA-256 `fffdbf6b659dc26cc0cf9193f38abcfea9f1cf52e489537d5fd51a3ed97fd464`, 85,641 bytes. Both downloads were verified against their uploaded bytes.

### Rules findings

Neither chess.js 1.4.0 nor chessops 0.15.1 meets the full accepted contract alone. Both support useful legal-move, checkmate, and stalemate operations in the selected fixtures. The application must own strict orthodox FEN/current-state validation, exact counter and declared-right preservation, specific rule explanations, repetition history, adjudication order, Undo, clocks, and response fencing.

The probes reproduced unsafe acceptance or normalization of some invalid FEN settings. chess.js repetition misses the third occurrence in the sampled custom starts with ineffective imported en-passant metadata. At halfmove 100, checkmate and its fifty-move draw predicate can both be true, so the controller must give checkmate precedence. These are bounded observed cases, not a claim that ordinary legality universally fails.

A complete exploration of a locked-pawn-wall fixture reached 768 states and 3,808 legal transitions with no check, mate, pawn move, or disagreement between libraries. Both libraries' material helpers still failed to identify the dead position. An asymmetric wall fixture also distinguishes global deadness from one side's inability to mate.

CHA-Solver 3.0.0 is an MIT-licensed candidate for further investigation. Eight native Windows queries produced four unwinnable verdicts and four cooperative mating witnesses, replayed in both JS libraries. Its source includes an explicit unknown result and search limits. No browser/WASM build, general completeness proof, or mobile resource bound was established. This research does not resolve exact adjudication for every allowed custom position.

### Board and licenses

cm-chessboard has relevant keyboard/form, readable-board, and explicit promotion/focus mechanisms; gchessboard is another credible accessible starting point. react-chessboard and Chessground require more application-owned complete screen-reader interaction. None passed native browser or assistive-technology acceptance in this research. Preserve the approved Classic workspace.

chess.js is BSD-2-Clause; cm-chessboard and several other candidates are MIT. chessops and Chessground require GPL-compatible distribution of a combined covered frontend. Piece/marker art has separate terms, including CC BY-SA and optional NonCommercial assets. Preserve actual shipped notices and avoid presenting the complete dependency/art bundle as MIT-only. The owner has since delegated the project's license default to architecture; no new license preference question is needed.

### Verification and remaining work

The coordinator reran the JS probe in an ignored evidence cache. All 12 grouped assertions passed, including the 768-state closure, and the complete resulting JSON exactly matched the recorded evidence. All 26 normalized checksums, 62 report reference definitions, and local linked files checked. The researcher also recorded eight native solver queries and four legal mating-witness replays; those native queries were not rerun by the coordinator. Research working tree remained clean.

The architecture ticket must resolve the exact-adjudication gap or obtain an explicit owner amendment. A question is now pending there about accepting documented rare exceptions versus retaining exact rules and researching a specialized solver. Neither option is presumed approved.

No production implementation, browser/AT acceptance, provider calls, credentials, paid usage, service provisioning, push, or running helper was created. This ticket resolves the factual investigation and leaves the product decision in [Choose the application architecture and data boundaries](https://linear.app/kamkm/issue/KHA-13/choose-the-application-architecture-and-data-boundaries).","attachments":[],"createdAt":"2026-10-16T00:35:27.946Z","updatedAt":"2026-10-16T00:35:27.920Z","parentId":null,"resolvedAt":null,"quotedText":null,"author":{"id":"45fdeba7-e6d5-4b71-912f-02932bc83a91","name":"khalil abdalmjeed"},"onBehalfOf":null}],"hasNextPage":false}
